Estimate nitrate leaching, topsoil denitrification and indirect N2O.

Source: R/n_balance_losses.R
calculate_n_leaching.Rd

Four methods for partitioning a nitrogen surplus into leached nitrate, denitrified nitrogen and nitrate retained in the soil profile.

"meisinger_drainage" (the default) is a transport-limited Meisinger cascade. Each year the surplus S and the nitrate the profile retained the year before, C_in (retained_carried_in_n_t), pass through it together: the nitrate available for transport is A = (S + C_in) (1 - d) (1 - a_cn), with d the topsoil denitrification share looked up from meisinger_denitrification by drainage class, soil organic matter class, fertiliser class and climate, and a_cn the carbon-to-nitrogen leaching attenuation. A transport factor f of the annual drainage D sets how much of A leaves the root zone, and the subsoil reduction red (subsoil_no3_reduction) acts on what leaves: no3_n_t = A f (1 - red), retained_profile_n_t = A (1 - f), and denitrification_n_t = S + C_in - no3_n_t - retained_profile_n_t (all the gaseous and subsoil sinks). The retained nitrate is next year's C_in on the same row key, so every row closes n_surplus_t + retained_carried_in_n_t = no3_n_t + denitrification_n_t + retained_profile_n_t.

"ipcc_fracleach" is the IPCC 2019 Tier 1 leached fraction, keyed on moisture_regime and water_regime, with every factor read from ipcc_2019_soil_n_ef: FracLEACH-(H) is 0.24 on wet rows and on dry irrigated rows and 0 on dry rainfed rows (IPCC 2019 Refinement Vol 4 Ch 11 Section 11.2.2.2 p. 11.25: 0.24 "for wet climates or in dry climate regions where irrigation (other than drip irrigation) is used"), and EF5 is 0.011 (Table 11.3 (Updated) p. 11.26). All irrigation is treated as non-drip, since no layer says which is drip: an upper-bound assumption for dry irrigated land. On wet and dry irrigated rows the rest of the surplus is booked as denitrification_n_t. On dry rainfed rows, where FracLEACH is 0, it is booked as retained_profile_n_t, nitrogen left in the soil profile, and denitrification_n_t is 0: FracLEACH says that surplus does not leach, not that it denitrifies, and no method here estimates its fate. That retained term is a flux of the year, not carried into the next one. Each row is stamped "ipcc_fracleach_wet", "ipcc_fracleach_dry_irrigated" or "ipcc_fracleach_dry_rainfed_retained". Eq. 11.10 and Table 11.3 define FracLEACH-(H) per kg of N added (F_SN + F_ON + F_PRP + F_CR + F_SOM), so it multiplies n_input_for_n2o_t, the same input set that prices direct N2O in build_nitrogen_balance(), not the surplus. "fracleach_surplus" applies the same fractions to n_surplus_t instead, the form before whep#1535: a surplus-based deviation from the IPCC definition, kept selectable for comparison, stamped "fracleach_surplus_wet" and so on. Under both, no3_n_t + denitrification_n_t + retained_profile_n_t equals n_surplus_t.

"image_gnm" is the root-zone leaching and denitrification of IMAGE-GNM (Beusen et al. 2015, Geosci. Model Dev. 8:4045-4067, doi:10.5194/gmd-8-4045-2015, eqs. 8-14, pp. 4051-4052, and Table 2, p. 4053). Surface runoff first carries off surface_runoff_n_t, a share of the year's nitrogen input (eq. 9). The budget left leaches in the share f_leach, no3_n_t = f_leach (n_surplus_t - surface_runoff_n_t) (eq. 10), and the rest of it denitrifies (f_den = 1 - f_leach), with f_leach = [1 - min(f_climate + f_text + f_drain + f_soc, 1)] f_landuse (eq. 11). The water that sets the root-zone residence time is the part of the total runoff runoff_mm that surface runoff does not carry off (eq. 5); drainage_mm is not read. On grassland and natural land with a total runoff below 3 mm/yr no water moves the surplus, which is held as inactive N in retained_profile_n_t. Eroded soil carries erosion_n_t from the soil's own organic nitrogen (eq. 8), which no budget pays for. See the IMAGE-GNM section under Details. IMAGE-GNM carries no nitrate from year to year, so every row with water closes max(n_surplus_t, surface_runoff_n_t) = surface_runoff_n_t + no3_n_t + denitrification_n_t, and every row without it retained_profile_n_t = max(n_surplus_t, 0).

Usage

calculate_n_leaching(
  x,
  drainage_mm = NULL,
  method = c("meisinger_drainage", "ipcc_fracleach", "fracleach_surplus", "image_gnm"),
  transport = c("swat_mixing", "swat_uniform", "burns", "unlimited"),
  none_class = c("retention", "waterlogged"),
  carry_over_by = NULL,
  initial_pool = c("steady_state", "zero"),
  example = FALSE
)

Source

IPCC (2019) 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Vol 4, Ch 11, Section 11.2.2.2, p. 11.25 (FracLEACH-(H)) and Table 11.3 (Updated), p. 11.26 (EF5). Beusen, A. H. W., Van Beek, L. P. H., Bouwman, A. F. et al. (2015). Coupling global models for hydrology and nutrient loading to simulate nitrogen and phosphorus retention in surface water - description of IMAGE-GNM and analysis of performance. Geosci. Model Dev. 8, 4045-4067. doi:10.5194/gmd-8-4045-2015 . The transport sources are cited under Details.

Arguments

x

A tibble with n_surplus_t. method = "meisinger_drainage" requires fert_type, climate, irrig_cat, land_use, cn_input (may be NA), tillage (checked only for synthetic rows), som_share and the soil columns its transport reads (see Details), plus year with carry_over_by; method = "ipcc_fracleach" requires moisture_regime ("wet" or "dry"), on dry rows water_regime ("rainfed" or "irrigated"), and n_input_for_n2o_t, the N added in IPCC Eq. 11.10; "fracleach_surplus" requires the first two; method = "image_gnm" requires n_input_std_t, nh3_n_t, area_ha, runoff_mm (the year's total runoff, mm), surface_runoff_fraction, slope_m_per_km (both from read_image_gnm_runoff()), land_use ("Cropland", "Grassland" or "Natural"), temp_c_annual_mean, soil_field_capacity, soil_wilting_point, soil_texture_class, soil_drainage_class and soil_organic_carbon_pct, and no surface_runoff_n_t (see Details).

drainage_mm

A numeric vector aligned to x's rows giving annual drainage (mm), or a single string naming a column of x to use instead. Kept as a separate argument (rather than a static x column) because in the full pipeline it flows in from Module A's gridded water balance. Read by "meisinger_drainage" only.

method

"meisinger_drainage" (default), "ipcc_fracleach", "fracleach_surplus" or "image_gnm".

transport

The transport factor of "meisinger_drainage": "swat_mixing" (default), "swat_uniform", "burns" or "unlimited".

none_class

How "meisinger_drainage" prices Meisinger's None drainage class: "retention" (default) or "waterlogged".

carry_over_by

Character vector of the columns that key a row across years (every key column but year), or NULL (default) to treat each row as a single year.

initial_pool

The nitrate a key's first year of "meisinger_drainage" starts with: "steady_state" (default), the pool of that year's fluxes repeated, or "zero".

example

If TRUE, return a small fixture instead of computing from x. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

x with no3_n_t, denitrification_n_t, retained_profile_n_t, n2o_indirect_no3_n_t and method_leaching appended, plus retained_carried_in_n_t under "meisinger_drainage" and "image_gnm", and surface_runoff_n_t and erosion_n_t under "image_gnm".

Details

Transport factor

transport selects f(D), with D the annual drainage (mm), h the root-zone depth root_depth_cm, phi the porosity soil_porosity and theta_fc the volumetric field capacity soil_field_capacity:

  • "swat_mixing" (default): the SWAT well-mixed layer, f = 1 - exp(-D / ((1 - theta_e) phi h)) with h in mm and the anion exclusion fraction theta_e = 0.5 (Neitsch et al. 2011, SWAT 2009 Theoretical Documentation, TR-406, eqs. 4:2.1.2 to 4:2.1.8, pp. 269-270; theta_e default from the SWAT Input/Output File Documentation, Version 2012, ch. 22, p. 304). The source equation is daily; applied to nitrate present before the year drains, with no other exit, the daily shares compound exactly to this form on the year's drainage, so the annual form assumes the surplus is in the root zone before the drainage season and that lateral flow is negligible.

  • "swat_uniform": the same daily equation for a surplus that arrives in proportion to the drainage through the year, integrated exactly: f_new = 1 - (1 - exp(-D / M)) / (D / M), M = (1 - theta_e) phi h, for the surplus, and the "swat_mixing" f for the carried pool, which is in the profile before the year drains. It bounds the input timing from the other side: on 2010 LPJmL monthly seepage, an explicit monthly iteration with equal monthly inputs gives a surplus-weighted mean within 2 percentage points of it (root zones of 30 to 150 cm).

  • "burns": Burns' displacement for a solute incorporated uniformly through the root zone, f = (P / (P + theta_fc))^(h / 2), with P the drainage and h the depth, both in cm (Burns 1976, J. Agric. Sci. 86:305-313, doi:10.1017/S0021859600054769).

  • "unlimited": no transport limit, f = 1 wherever the row drains: the Meisinger cascade as it stood before transport was added, kept to measure what the transport limit changes. Nothing is retained on a drained row.

Every constant is read from n_attenuation_constants. The columns a transport reads must be present and non-missing on every row: "swat_mixing" and "swat_uniform" read root_depth_cm and soil_porosity, "burns" root_depth_cm and soil_field_capacity, and "unlimited" neither.

Zero drainage and deep vadose storage

Where D <= 0 nothing is transported (f = 0). The year's own available nitrate S (1 - d) (1 - a_cn) is retained, and the carried pool C_in is held as deep vadose storage: it is neither denitrified nor leached that year and re-enters the cascade in the next year that drains (Walvoord et al. 2003, Science, doi:10.1126/science.1086435; Ascott et al. 2017, Nat. Commun., doi:10.1038/s41467-017-01321-w). Such rows carry the field vadose_storage.

Drainage classes

Drainage and soil organic matter bins are matched with the source's strictly-open s_min < s < s_max filter: a value exactly on a shared bin edge, or below the lowest bin, matches no bin and aborts via the unmatched-row check rather than being pulled into an adjacent bin. The top drainage bin is open: drainage of 3,000 mm and above takes the Very_high share. Meisinger's None class (drainage below 0.1 mm/yr) is set by none_class: "retention" (default) takes the Very_low row's share, so what does not denitrify is retained or stored; "waterlogged" keeps the table's literal None rows, which denitrify the whole surplus.

Manure/organic rows (fert_cat == "Manure", i.e. every fert_type other than "Synthetic") always join the Meisinger table's tillage == "Not_specified" row regardless of x$tillage. Synthetic rows join on x$tillage, but only "Tillage" exists in the source's synthetic block: a synthetic row with tillage == "No_tillage" aborts. A pooled "Excreta" row (excreta of every species, as build_n_inputs() emits it) reads the subsoil reduction of subsoil_no3_reduction, which gives "Excreta_cattle_monog" and "Excreta_other" the same value in every class; were they to differ, the row aborts (whep_leaching_excreta_species).

Carry-over across years

With carry_over_by, rows are threaded per key in year order: each row's C_in is the retained_profile_n_t of its key's previous row. A key's first row starts at the steady state of that year's fluxes, C_in = S r / (1 - r), where the share of the pool's input that stays is (1 - d) (1 - a_cn) (1 - f), written r (field initial_pool_steady_state; under "swat_uniform" the surplus feeds the pool with (1 - d) (1 - a_cn) (1 - f_new) instead, so C_in = S (1 - d) (1 - a_cn) (1 - f_new) / (1 - r)). initial_pool = "zero" starts every key empty instead (field initial_pool_zero), the lower bound of a run with no legacy nitrate: in a one-year run under a transport other than "swat_uniform" it leaches 1 - r times what the steady state does. A key whose first year does not drain has no finite steady state and starts at 0 (field initial_vadose_zero) under either. Later rows carry the field carried_pool. A key absent from a year of the run keeps its pool on the key: the pool is neither moved to another key nor dropped, and re-enters when the key reappears. The row whose pool waits that way, the key's last row before a run year it lacks, carries the field pool_held_absent_key. Over a run, the sum of n_surplus_t equals the sums of no3_n_t and denitrification_n_t, plus each key's last retained_profile_n_t, minus each key's first retained_carried_in_n_t. Without carry_over_by every row is its own key's first and only year.

method_leaching joins these fields with ;: meisinger_drainage; the transport; none_retention or none_waterlogged; the pool field; and, optionally, vadose_storage and pool_held_absent_key.

IMAGE-GNM

method = "image_gnm" follows Beusen et al. (2015), eqs. 8-14 (pp. 4051-4052) and Table 2 (p. 4053). Where the paper is silent or ambiguous, or disagrees with the code, it follows the authors' model code published with the paper (doi:10.5194/gmd-8-4045-2015-supplement, N_model/trunk/tools/, the code that produced their results), as noted below.

  • f_climate = f_K T_r (eq. 12), with f_K = 7.94e12 exp(-74830 / (R K)) (eq. 13), R = 8.3144 J/(mol K) and K the mean annual temperature temp_c_annual_mean + 273.15 (the authors' code adds 273). f_K is bounded at 1, as in the authors' code (line 97); the bound binds above about 30 degC.

  • T_r = tawc / q_eff years (eq. 14). tawc is the total available water capacity of the top 1 m, (soil_field_capacity - soil_wilting_point) x 1,000 mm. The source takes the top 1 m "or less if thinner"; WHEP has no soil-thickness layer, so the full 1 m is used everywhere. q_eff is the excess water flow of eq. 5 (p. 4049), the water that infiltrates and recharges shallow and deep groundwater, as the authors' code computes it (n_soil_denitrification.py lines 356, 376 and 399): q_eff = (1 - f_qsro(landuse) f_qsro) q_tot, the total runoff less the share surface runoff carries off, with the f_qsro(landuse) and f_qsro of eq. 9 below. q_tot is runoff_mm, the year's total runoff: LPJmL's mrunoff.nc (read_lpjml_hydrology() "runoff"), which holds the groundwater outflow the deep seepage feeds, as the authors' pnet, the hydrology model's total runoff, does. Below 3 mm/yr the authors' code takes no water through the root zone (lines 341-344; minimal_soil_infiltration = 3.0 mm/yr, parameters_history_100.ini line 204), so on cropland q_tot is 0 there; grassland and natural land below it never reach eq. 14 (see the inactive N below). Where q_eff is 0 the authors' code takes T_r = 100 years (trzd(), lines 179-182).

  • On cropland T_r is at most 1 year, as in the authors' code (lines 377-378: crops must have enough water, for example from irrigation). The printed sentence (p. 4052) reads as raising a T_r below 1 to 1 on dry agricultural land; the code lowers every cropland T_r above 1 to 1, and the code is followed.

  • f_text, f_drain and f_soc are read from image_gnm_leaching_factors (Table 2) on soil_texture_class, soil_drainage_class and the topsoil organic carbon soil_organic_carbon_pct (% by weight; each organic-carbon class holds its lower bound, as in the authors' class code). f_landuse is 1 on "Cropland" and 0.36 on "Grassland" and "Natural" (p. 4052, citing Keuskamp et al. 2012).

  • surface_runoff_n_t is N_sro,rec of eq. 9 (p. 4052), the nitrogen surface runoff carries off from the year's inputs before the budget leaches: f_cal f_qsro(landuse) f_qsro N_inp, with f_cal = 0.3 and f_qsro(landuse) 1 on cropland, 0.25 on grassland and 0.125 on natural vegetation (Table 3, p. 4056; the authors' code, n_surface_runoff.py lines 98, 114 and 128, uses the same values). f_qsro, the product f_qsro(slope) f_qsro(texture) of eqs. 3-4 (p. 4049), is the column surface_runoff_fraction: the authors' own 0.5-degree layer, which their code reads instead of computing eq. 4 (see read_image_gnm_runoff()). N_inp follows the authors' code: on cropland and grassland the input net of ammonia, n_input_std_t - nh3_n_t, floored at 0 (n_surface_runoff.py lines 57-58, 96 and 112); on natural vegetation the surplus n_surplus_t, floored at 0 (line 128). In build_nitrogen_balance() n_input_std_t is biological fixation, excreta, liquid and solid manure, synthetic fertiliser, human N applied to land and deposition: it includes human N applied to land and excludes N mineralised from soil organic matter and recycled crop residues. The authors' input is the year's N applied to or deposited on the land, manure, fertiliser, fixation and deposition (lines 57-58), the N exposed to surface runoff before it enters the soil. Human N applied to land reaches the surface as manure does, so it is kept; mineralised soil N is released inside the soil and recycled residues return N the crop took from the same soil, so neither is a fresh input at the surface. Surface runoff is a share of the input, so it can exceed the surplus; eq. 10 is then negative, and the authors' code sets the budget to 0 (lines 106, 122 and 136), as here: nothing leaches or denitrifies and the row books max(n_surplus_t, surface_runoff_n_t). A negative surplus (a deficit, which build_nitrogen_balance() never passes) is floored at a budget of 0 the same way: nothing leaches or denitrifies, and the surface runoff is still booked.

  • Inactive N. Where the total runoff runoff_mm is below 3 mm/yr, the authors' code sets the grassland and natural balances to 0 before surface runoff and denitrification and books them as N no water transports (n_nowater.py lines 31-46, called from N-model.py lines 210-214); cropland is left alone, "for arable land it is assumed that there is always enough water" (line 19). Here that N is retained_profile_n_t = max(n_surplus_t, 0), and nothing leaches or denitrifies. Surface runoff then reads the zeroed balance: natural land runs off nothing, and grassland a share of balance + uptake, which is its uptake alone (n_surface_runoff.py line 96), here the input net of ammonia less the surplus, max(0, n_input_std_t - nh3_n_t - n_surplus_t). That runoff is booked beside the inactive N, not taken from it. Under build_nitrogen_balance(), whose surplus counts the N mineralised from soil organic matter as an input and soil organic matter sequestration as an output while n_input_std_t counts neither, this proxy (where the balance is in surplus) is the crop product, the used, bedding and burnt residue and the grazed forage, plus the sequestration less the mineralisation: uptake net of the soil organic matter terms.

  • erosion_n_t is N_sro,mem of eq. 8 (p. 4052), the nitrogen of soil lost to erosion, computed as the authors' code does (n_erosion.py lines 47-55 and 88-135): an erodibility (-1.5 + 17 / (1 + exp(2.3 - 6.1 S / 1000))) times a texture factor (1.5 on medium and fine, 0.5 on the others), with S the median slope slope_m_per_km; a soil loss of 1,151, 99 and 29 t per km2 per unit erodibility on cropland, grassland and natural vegetation over area_ha; and N = soil loss x soil_organic_carbon_pct / C:N, with C:N 12, 14 and 14 (p. 4052). area_ha drives it: in build_nitrogen_balance() it is the physical agricultural land of ag_land_support, or, where that cannot be derived, the crop's harvested area, which counts multi-cropped land once per crop and so overstates erosion there. The paper subtracts the whole of eq. 8 in eq. 10; the authors' code subtracts only the runoff from the recent inputs and adds the eroded N to the river load (N-model.py lines 233-243 and 307), so erosion_n_t is reported and taken from no budget.

  • IMAGE-GNM keeps no root-zone nitrate from one year to the next: retained_carried_in_n_t is 0 by construction, retained_profile_n_t is 0 on every row with water and is not carried into the next year, and transport, none_class and carry_over_by do not apply.

Two parts of the authors' code are not reproduced. Its separate water capacities of dominant and suitable soils, because WHEP has one soil per cell. And its f_soc, which it interpolates linearly from 0 at 0% to 0.3 at 6% organic carbon; the printed classes of Table 2 are used instead.

method_leaching is image_gnm;tawc_top_1m, followed where they apply by runoff_below_min_infiltration (a non-zero runoff_mm below 3 mm/yr set to 0), no_excess_water_residence_100yr (q_eff of 0), crop_residence_cap_1yr (a cropland T_r above 1 year held at 1), temperature_effect_cap_1 (an f_K above 1 held at 1), nowater_inactive_n (a grassland or natural row below 3 mm/yr, whose surplus is inactive N; such a row carries none of the three fields before it), negative_surplus_budget_0 (a negative n_surplus_t, leaving a budget of 0) and surface_runoff_exceeds_budget (a surface runoff above a non-negative surplus, leaving a budget of 0), joined with ;.

Errors

  • whep_missing_leaching_driver (also whep_absent_input): a driver column the transport reads is absent or holds a missing value, or drainage_mm is absent or missing.

  • whep_leaching_driver_value: a non-positive root_depth_cm, a porosity or field capacity outside (0, 1], or a drainage at or below -0.1 mm.

  • whep_leaching_carry_key: carry_over_by names an absent column, x has no year, or a key occurs twice in one year.

For method = "image_gnm":

  • whep_missing_leaching_driver (also whep_absent_input): a column it reads, runoff_mm among them, is absent or holds a missing value.

  • whep_leaching_driver_value: a field capacity outside (0, 1], a wilting point outside (0, field capacity), a negative organic carbon, slope, area, input or ammonia, a non-finite temperature, a non-finite runoff_mm or one at or below water_flux_floor_mm of n_attenuation_constants (-0.1 mm; LPJmL's float residues just below 0 pass and fall under the 3 mm/yr threshold), or a surface runoff fraction outside [0, 1].

  • whep_gnm_runoff_supplied: x already holds surface_runoff_n_t, which "image_gnm" computes; drop it rather than have it overwritten.

  • whep_leaching_class_value: a texture, drainage or land-use label image_gnm_leaching_factors does not hold. The authors' code books an unknown texture or drainage class as 0; here it aborts, because a class that cannot be read is not a class.

For method = "ipcc_fracleach", a missing or invalid moisture_regime aborts as in calculate_soil_n2o(), and a dry row without a water_regime aborts (whep_missing_water_regime for an absent column, whep_water_regime_value for a missing or unknown value, naming the count): dry irrigated and dry rainfed land leach 0.24 and 0 of their surplus, so a dry row of unknown regime has no defensible fraction. Wet rows need no water_regime. "fracleach_surplus" checks the same. transport, none_class, carry_over_by and initial_pool do not apply to either.

Under "ipcc_fracleach" leaching is capped at n_surplus_t, so it never exceeds the nitrogen left after crop uptake. IPCC Tier 1 has no such cap; rows where it binds carry the suffix "_capped_surplus" on their stamp (e.g. "ipcc_fracleach_wet_capped_surplus"). A missing n_input_for_n2o_t column, or a missing value in it, aborts (whep_missing_n_added, whep_n_added_na): read as zero it would leach nothing while the partition still closed.

Examples

calculate_n_leaching(example = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   n_surplus_t moisture_regime n_input_for_n2o_t no3_n_t denitrification_n_t
#>         <dbl> <chr>                       <dbl>   <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1          60 wet                           100      24                  36
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: retained_profile_n_t <dbl>, n2o_indirect_no3_n_t <dbl>,
#> #   method_leaching <chr>
